5.description:
Oct Second Headquarters: A Well-Deserved Victory
The Oct Second Headquarters competition was a well-deserved victory, as our idea 
stood out as the most distinctive and superior among all the proposals. We skillfully 
integrated various functions into a single building, effectively solving circulation issues 
and showcasing Rocco's remarkable abilities. The architectural design capitalized on 
Kunming's local climate, incorporating natural ventilation to reduce energy consumption. 
Unfortunately, financial constraints led to modifications in the building's form, and the 
project came to a halt when our collaborating partner went bankrupt during construction.
Despite setbacks, our design showcased deep functionality and sustainability 
understanding, blending them seamlessly into a harmonious composition. Although 
the project remains unfinished, the lessons learned will shape future endeavors. I am 
determined to continue pursuing excellence in architecture, overcoming challenges, and 
creating exceptional architectural marvels. The Oct Second Headquarters, regardless of 
its completion status, stands as a testament to our creativity and innovative thinking.
Personal Reflections

7.description:
OCT is the guru in tourism and cultural industry, advocating innovation and high quality living. Known as the  “City of 
Eternal Spring”, Kunming is filled with nat¬ural wonders and historical sites.

8.description:
Given the mild climate of Kunming, natural ventilation for public spaces is made possible. Exter¬nally, green walls and 
planting migrate upward from ground level, garnishing the cityscape.

9.description: Elevated public spaces are hung in mid-levels, enhancing the headquarters distinctive form.

10.description:
We propose to rearrange the southern residential towers to create a coherent master layout plan. At the 
centre of the site, the hotel and service apartment are placed in low zone facing east and west respectively, 
with the headquarters office stacked above, and each has its own distinct entrance.

11.description:
HUAWAI-TONGMAN is an exceptional school that proudly 
embraces its local cultural heritage while fostering 
a strong connection to global perspectives. Their 
ambitious goal is to build a campus that is entirely unique, 
challenging architects to think beyond traditional designs 
and create something truly groundbreaking. 
To achieve this, we explored a diverse array of spatial 
arrangements, carefully considering how each could 
enhance both functionality and aesthetics. The result is a 
remarkably cohesive structure that defies the conventional 
appearance of a school, offering instead a bold, innovative 
environment that feels fresh and forward-thinking. 
This distinctive design has given rise to a variety of 
extraordinary spaces, each with its own character and 
purpose, sparking creativity and interaction among 
students and educators. Far from typical classrooms 
and hallways, these spaces encourage exploration, 
collaboration, and inspiration, aligning perfectly with the 
school’s vision of blending cultural pride with international 
openness. 
This project represents a significant architectural 
milestone, redefining what an educational institution can 
be. 
Personal Reflections

12.description:
I see the development of the massing model as creating a cohesive visual system that emphasizes its 
impact in space. This approach ensures each element enhances overall visual strength and harmony.



I carefully considered proportions and shapes, making adjustments for balance and precision. The main 
mass serves as the foundation, providing stability and setting the design's tone, while additional dynamic 
elements add interest and depth. This clear hierarchy creates a striking visual effect and ensures function­
al harmony. Ultimately, the goal is to create an engaging and practical architectural model.

13.description:
The design contrasts primary and secondary masses, making the main volume the visual focus while 
the secondary masses provide support, creating clear layers. The combination of solid and transparent 
spaces balances enclosed and open areas, allowing light and air to activate the environment. Vertical 
and horizontal contrasts enrich the form and enhance stability and site integration. The use of white and 
beige materials reinforces the hierarchy and clearly communicates the design intent.

14.description:
We aim to balance functionality and aesthetics, creating spaces that support diverse educational activ­
ities and energize the campus. The design responds to the concept of being "more Chinese and more 
global." As an art of problem-solving, architecture enhances well-being through meaningful spaces 
that uplift both spirit and environment.

16.description:
1. Research shows that focusing the layout on this plot effec­
tively addresses image and functionality.
2. Opening the north-south volume reduces bulky massing 
and improves ventilation.
3.Dormitories are placed in the upper area, while large spac­
es are located beneath the atrium and football field.
4.Integrating the overall elevation design to highlight a 
Chinese aesthetic.
5.Enriching the internal green public spaces.

17.description:
Upon entering the covered atrium, you are welcomed by a continuous vertical 
space. The upper level features interactive living areas, while the lower level 
includes the auditorium lobby and access to the outdoor atrium. The vertical 
facade design on both sides enhances depth. This spacious area supports 
large events and protects them from the weather.
Entering the covered atrium, you encounter a seamless vertical space. The 
upper level has interactive living areas, while the lower level includes the au­
ditorium lobby and access to the outdoor atrium. The vertical facade design 
enhances depth. This spacious area supports events and shields them from 
the weather.
As you move from the covered atrium to the outdoor atrium, the building 
frames the northern landscape and connects to the west sports field, creating 
an interactive space with the library. Unlike the covered atrium, the outdoor 
atrium enjoys natural ventilation, allowing for closer interaction with the sur­
roundings.

18.description:
Greater-Bay Science Forum: An Invitational Competition
As an architect speaking from a first-person perspective, 
I would like to convey that at its core, this competition 
revolves around the exploration of innovative architectural 
forms. It is a challenge to see who can create the most 
extraordinary and distinctive design. As architects tasked 
with creating a building that serves a simple function and 
can be seamlessly integrated into various volumes, our 
primary objective is to meet the functional requirements 
while satisfying Rocco's design aspirations.
When contemplating waterfront architecture, the 
immediate association is often with curved forms. 
However, since we are not Zaha and cannot compete 
directly in their forte, we decided to approach the design 
from a different angle - the concept of a carrier. Our 
intention was to evoke a sense of movement, as if the 
building is propelling forward at high speed. This imagery 
not only aligns well with the theme of technology but also 
adds a dynamic element to the overall composition.
Regrettably, our design did not secure a place among the 
top three winners. The chosen scheme was deemed rather 
ordinary and failed to capture the essence of innovation. 
Such unexpected outcomes are not uncommon in the 
world of architecture, where subjective judgments and 
varying tastes play a significant role in the final selection 
process.
Personal Reflections

19.description:
建筑肌理蕴藏严谨的逻辑模数，并与江边元素呼应，再一次呼应方案主旨。
通过创造极具标志性的线条勾勒，连通了两大版块的公共性，同时在西侧区域创造出富有特
色的公共空间。
考虑到位处焦门及上横沥水道交汇处，本体量通过斜面的处理，将建筑以独占鳌头之气势立
于明珠湾，创造明珠湾区域的焦点。
在东西两个体量内创造不同空间体验的空间，将入口广场及各中庭空间巧妙镶嵌其中。
依据私密性，可达性等客观要求及功能体量的分布，在对内和对外区域之间创造出贯穿场地
南北的公共交通流线，将科学家公寓和科创中心与学术中心和科技馆划分开。同时，在场地
东西方向打造建筑整体的东西向对称轴线，贯穿场地始末。
在地面空间规划上，本项目整体划分对外及对内两大功能版块，对内，则是位于场地西南西
北角的科学家公寓及科创中心；对外则是位于东南和东北位置的科技馆和学术中心，科技馆
和学术中心面向东侧江景，以吻合其公共性。
The Permanent Venue of the Greater Bay Area Science Forum, situated in the prominent Pearl Bay area, is a prestigious project designed 
around three core principles:
1. Scientific Precision and Innovation: The architecture should reflect a sharp, cutting-edge image that showcases the forum’s dedication 
to scientific excellence.
2. Futuristic Design: The building must feature advanced construction techniques, exuding a bold, forward-looking aesthetic.
3. Regional Vibrancy: The design should highlight the unique cultural and dynamic spirit of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater 
Bay Area.
Together, these elements create a landmark that serves as both a center for intellectual collaboration and a celebration of the region’s 
identity and ambition.

20.description:
The building's form is shaped by functional needs, creating distinct identities. The scientists' apartments 
and innovation center, designed for internal use, adopt a rigorous and grand style. In contrast, the 
academic center and science museum, feature sculptural forms with a dynamic, soaring momentum. 
These contrasting styles connect seamlessly in mid-air, transitioning from disciplined to dynamic in one 
fluid gesture.

21.description:
科技馆位于东南角的三至五楼，占地三层，参观者和使用者
可以通过中庭南侧的连续电梯进入到各个展厅之中，浏览最
前沿的科学学术成果等内容。
学术中心位于东北角的三至五楼，占地三层，使用者可以通
过中庭南侧的连续电梯进入到各个会场之中，参加在这里举
办的各类论坛。
科学家公寓位于场地的西南角二层以上位置，确保了公寓内
拥有充足的采光，同时也拥有最好的江景。其配套设置则主
要布置于首层位置，以确保其便利性。
科创中心位于场地的西北角，可以欣赏场地北侧的江景。其
在首层拥有独立的出入口和大堂。

22.description:
Embodies the spirit of scientific 
exploration,

Showcases the exquisite 
craftsmanship of architecture,

Pays tribute to the sacred 
solemnity of research.

23.description:
The main entrance of the Academic Center and Science Museum is located on the 
ground floor of the west side. It features high-transparency laminated glass with 
a standard curved design, and the corridors on both sides form an entrance plaza 
distinct from the east side. This creates a premier international hub for scientific 
cooperation, embodying technological civilization.

24.description:
The design draws inspiration from the history of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, 
rooted in its origins as the starting point of the Maritime Silk Road. Using ships and carriages as formal 
motifs and technology as the foundation, the architecture conveys a dynamic aesthetic of readiness and 
breaking through challenges.

25.description:
The site is located at the central financial district of Futian, Shenzhen with a stunning 
view of the Shenzhen Golf Club at the west.
The concepts will be discussed in detail in the subsequent pages. Here, I would like to 
share my personal reflections as the lead designer of this project.
This project presents both opportunities and challenges. The location holds great 
potential, but the difficulties arise from the diverse interests and approaches of the 
stakeholders in safeguarding their own benefits.
I acknowledge that no project is perfect, and mistakes are inevitable. However, if there 
were effective oversight mechanisms in place or if project managers approached non-
compliance issues with impartiality, many of the visible errors could have been proactively 
addressed. This is merely a suggestion.
There has been a comparison made, likening this building to a child that must endure 
hardships to transform into a swan. Yet, it is important to note that the ugly duckling 
becomes a swan because it was inherently a swan from the beginning, not as a result of 
undergoing genetic mutations due to suffering. Promoting the education of misfortune 
(hardship) only fosters self-doubt and insecurity. It is crucial to never believe that 
misfortune (hardship) is inherently beneficial.
Personal Reflections

29.description:
Using a central core design fails to distinguish the varying value of 
each side of the tower and underutilizes the expansive golf course 
views.
With a split core configuration, the lower zone connects to the 
urban green belt, while the upper zone maximizes exposure to the 
western golf course views.
The ventilated atrium in the lower zone introduces natural airflow, 
enhancing energy efficiency.
Using straightforward architectural techniques, the building's form 
is shaped, employing a three-part division for a sleeker proportion.
The recessed atrium in the upper zone brings panoramic views 
inside, allowing for optimal sharing of the stunning scenery.
The podium features a three-dimensional green facade, 
contributing to the urban landscape.

33.description:
This is a competition project that I completed with my 
colleagues. Unfortunately, we did not receive any awards, 
but I still believe it is worth including in my portfolio. 
Surprisingly, the winning proposal turned out to be a 
design that only involved graffiti on the exterior walls, 
while the museum itself is now being transformed into 
an exhibition hall showcasing national achievements. 
Therefore, I find it significant to commemorate this once-
existing trace.
Although I personally find it foolish and absurd that the 
act of transforming the museum is being disguised under 
the justification of using a noise barrier, as required by the 
building regulations in Hong Kong, it also reflects, to some 
extent, the relatively robust regulatory system in place.
Personal Reflections

37.description:
Despite multiple rounds of mid-term communication with 
the client, we still lost the competition. They said the 
reason was that they did not want the design to be too 
flashy.
This building actually fulfilled the criteria of being easily 
realizable and having distinctive features. It's a shame we 
didn't win this competition. Interestingly, the client's boss 
later passed away, and after that, they commissioned us to 
do the interior design work.
Personal Reflections

38.description:
This was a project I actively participated in, contributing 
to the design and assisting with the development 
of a proposal for the Oct bid site. Although I did not 
continue my involvement with the project after it was 
awarded, I take pride in knowing that the performance 
center has been successfully constructed. This project 
marked my first foray into theater design, allowing me 
to delve into aspects such as streamlined layouts and 
spatial arrangements. As a result, I gained a fundamental 
understanding of the unique considerations involved in 
designing such architectural spaces.
Regrettably, one of the key associates responsible for 
the project did not meet expectations, leading to a 
significant number of glaring mistakes that were visible 
upon completion. This experience has underscored the 
importance of exercising caution and diligence when 
selecting the primary individuals responsible for a project. 
It serves as a valuable lesson in the significance of having 
a competent and reliable team in place to ensure the 
successful execution of architectural endeavors.
Personal Reflections

39.description:
Although we did not emerge as winners in the 
competition, this particular challenge provided me with 
the opportunity to broaden my understanding of sports 
architecture. It became evident that theaters and sports 
centers are two distinct entities, each with its own 
distinct emotional ambiance, contextual requirements, 
and operational strategies. To address this dichotomy, a 
decision was made to physically separate these functions 
in the design.
In this architectural masterpiece, characterized by its 
striking Rococo features, the connecting platform that 
spans between the theater and the sports center takes 
on a unique role. It serves as a dynamic stage, not only 
facilitating the seamless transition between these 
contrasting spaces but also creating a vibrant urban 
experience. The platform becomes a nexus, where 
spectators and participants can gather, interact, and 
immerse themselves in the energy of the city. It symbolizes 
the harmonious coexistence of art and athleticism, 
blending the elegance of theater with the dynamism of 
sports.
Personal Reflections

41.description:
This is a mixed-use project that encompasses 
office buildings, apartments, and commercial 
spaces across four plots. The commercial element 
is heavily influenced by market demands, and 
given the prime location in Shenzhen, the need 
for vertical development is particularly pressing.

The two towers depicted in the design are high-end 
apartments that should convey a public building image 
while encouraging interaction. To meet the strict room 
mix requirements, the facade features wavy horizontal 
lines that soften layout differences and create a textural 
connection with the surrounding area.
Personal Reflections

42.description:
This project is commissioned by the owner to focus solely 
on the facade. With the main structure already completed 
and the complexities of government regulations, there's 
limited room for adjustments to the building massing. I’ve 
chosen a design language that emphasizes solid surfaces. 
Unfortunately, the Qianhai management department has 
many directives that prevent us from fully realizing the 
architect's and owner's vision. Despite these challenges, 
we dedicated considerable effort to perfecting the facade 
details.
Personal Reflections

43.description:
This was a project I actively participated in, contributing 
to the design and assisting with the development of a 
prThis is actually a competition with a lot of restrictions. 
Within the relatively small site, we need to cram in all the 
required functions, and the possible layout variations are 
not many. We chose a more aggressive 45-degree diagonal 
treatment. Unfortunately, the client probably already had 
a preferred scheme in mind. This competition was won by 
AEDAS.
The strength of this competition entry likely lies in the 
relatively novel layout strategy employed for the podium 
levels, even though this approach is not very common. 
Considering that the client seemed to be somewhat 
inexperienced, we felt it was still worth attempting this 
more experimental design.
Personal Reflections

44.description:
This is a 300-meter-high tower in Guangzhou, situated in 
the densely built area of Zhujiang New Town. It appears 
notably unremarkable; without post-processing in the 
photo, you might not even recognize it as the main 
subject. The design features exploded corners that don't 
align with its function, and the 45-degree angle in relation 
to the urban grid feels out of place. Of course, this 
isn't my design—I was only responsible for post-project 
coordination. A positive takeaway from this job is that it 
marks my record for the tallest building I've worked on.
Personal Reflections
